# Board Prep — Q2 Update

**Attendees:** Mira (CEO), Dev (CFO), Wei (Director of Eng), Sara (Head of Product), Lena (Head of Sales)

---

Mira: We have the board meeting in two weeks. The deck is two-thirds done. Today I want us to align on the three messages we want to land and identify the gaps in supporting data.

Dev: Top of the list — we want to land that we're on track to hit revenue plan despite the macroeconomic headwinds. Q2 is at 94% of plan with one month to go.

Mira: Lena, what's the bridge from 94% to plan?

Lena: We have three deals in late-stage negotiation that close the gap. Brightline Logistics is the largest — $480K ARR, contract under review. Two others worth combined $310K. If two of three close, we hit plan. If only one closes, we land at 96%.

Mira: We need to give the board a confidence interval, not a hope. Lena, can you put together a probability-weighted forecast on these three deals by end of next week?

Lena: I'll have the weighted forecast ready by Friday next week, with notes on what changes the weights.

Dev: Second message — we want to communicate that the unit economics are improving. Gross margin moved from 64% to 71% over the last three quarters. That's strong but the board will ask why.

Wei: That's mostly the infra optimization work the platform team did in Q1 and Q2. We can quantify it. I'll put together a one-pager on the cost-reduction initiatives — cloud-spend savings, query optimization, the hot-storage tiering — with dollar impact for each.

Mira: Wei, when can I have that?

Wei: End of next week.

Sara: Third message I'd like to make — product velocity. We shipped seven major features this half against a plan of six, and customer satisfaction on those features averages 4.4. That's a strong signal we should highlight.

Mira: Agreed. Sara, which feature do we want as the showcase in the deck? We need a brief story arc.

Sara: The analytics dashboard. It went from kickoff to ship in 11 weeks against a planned 14, has 64% adoption among paid users in the first month, and accounts for an estimated 18% of upsell conversations. I'll write up the story arc in two paragraphs and send it Tuesday.

Mira: Good. What are the gaps?

Dev: I'm uncomfortable with the cash runway slide. We're at fourteen months at current burn, but the assumptions on the next-round timing are stale. I want the board to see a refreshed scenario set — best, base, worst case for runway.

Mira: Dev, can you refresh the runway model by Wednesday next week?

Dev: I'll send the updated model on Wednesday.

Lena: One concern about the deck — the customer logo slide is out of date. Three of those logos churned over the last quarter. We should swap them.

Mira: Lena, send Sara the updated logo list and let's get it into the deck before the next draft. By Monday.

Lena: I'll have the list to Sara by Monday morning.

Sara: I'll incorporate the new logos into the deck same day.

Mira: One more — we should pre-meet with our lead investor before the formal board meeting to socialize the runway scenarios. Dev, can you set up a 30-minute prep with them next week?

Dev: I'll reach out to their EA today and set up a slot.

Mira: Recap. Lena: probability-weighted forecast on Brightline and the two other deals by Friday next week, plus updated customer logos to Sara by Monday morning. Wei: one-pager on cost-reduction initiatives with dollar impact by end of next week. Sara: two-paragraph analytics-dashboard story arc by Tuesday and incorporates the new logos same day Lena sends them. Dev: refreshed runway model with three scenarios by Wednesday next week, plus a 30-minute pre-meet with the lead investor scheduled. The three messages we're landing: on track to hit revenue plan, unit economics improving, product velocity above plan with strong adoption.

Sara: Got it.

Mira: Talk Tuesday.
